notes: M.G.L. c. 186 § 18 is Massachusetts' anti-retaliation (reprisal) statute. It makes a landlord liable for damages of 1 to 3 months' rent, or actual damages if greater, plus costs and attorney's fees, for reprisals against tenants who report code violations, take legal action, or organize. A notice of termination (except for nonpayment), a rent increase, or a substantial change in tenancy terms within six months of protected activity creates a rebuttable presumption of reprisal. It does not require a listed cause to evict, cap rent increases, or regulate deposits, fees, screening, or rent-setting software, so no rule was extracted under the six in-scope categories. A reviewer may decide whether retaliation protections should be tracked separately or folded into just_cause_eviction.
